mechanism_narrative: The continued improvement in transit, workplaces, and parks from t-3w to t-1w signals broader outing intensity that should keep retail and recreation rising over the next month. If people are already leaving home more for commuting and discretionary trips, retail visits should lag by 1-4 weeks and move upward.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the last 4 weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain above their t-0w levels for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When residential mobility stays elevated while workplaces remain depressed, more activity is being displaced into local errands rather than destination shopping, which lowers retail and recreation mobility over the next 1-2 weeks. The mechanism is a home-based substitution effect that suppresses discretionary retail trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above baseline and WORKPLACES staying below baseline throughout the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in transit stations mobility below the current t-0w level signals renewed transport constraint or risk aversion, and retail mobility will follow downward within one week. The claim is falsified if retail keeps improving after transit weakens sharply.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -42 after already being at or below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower in the next week after TRANSIT crosses below -42 from an already depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy mobility rebounds while parks stay weak, households are still doing necessary local trips but not extending them into discretionary shopping, so retail and recreation remains soft over the next four weeks. This mechanism predicts a flat-to-down retail path unless parks and transit recover together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM rises and PARKS remains below its t-1w level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in parks mobility is a warm-weather discretionary signal that typically precedes higher shopping and leisure activity within two weeks. If park use keeps increasing from the already improved t-1w and t-0w readings, retail mobility should move up soon after.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS rises for two more consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A partial normalization in workplaces combined with stable residential time indicates easing of constraints and a return to mixed-location routines that boosts retail visits over the next month. The signal is strongest when workplace mobility stops falling and moves back toward baseline.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns upward from a week-on-week decline and RESIDENTIAL stops rising
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean even after WORKPLACES turns upward and RESIDENTIAL flattens for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When transit is still deeply negative but parks are improving, people are substituting local outdoor activity for shopping trips, which delays retail recovery rather than accelerating it. Over the next one to two weeks, retail should stay weak unless transit also rebounds.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 while PARKS rises above -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the next week even though TRANSIT stays below -40 and PARKS continues to recover.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sequence of rising retail, transit, and workplace mobility through t-1w indicates a momentum regime that should keep retail mobility higher over the next four weeks. This is a persistence signal: recent gains in external activity propagate into continued discretionary footfall.
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the previous 28-day mean even though RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all showed recent week-on-week improvement.
